title: Electrical boundaries and referral
referencesAtStart: Official sources for this lesson: NSW Government, Electrical licences and credentials (last updated 23 June 2026); Energy Safe Victoria, Renewable energy licence questions (reviewed 4 June 2024); Energy Safe Victoria, Safely installing photovoltaic (PV) systems (reviewed 15 April 2025); Queensland Building and Construction Commission, When you need a QBCC licence (last reviewed 11 August 2021).
audience: Handyman workers and property maintenance workers who may encounter electrical faults or electrical tasks
learningOutcomes: Identify the electrical tasks that are treated as referral for a handyman, with the reason.
Describe the safe response to a suspected electrical fault found during other work.
State the licence positions recorded for electrical work in each state, without implying any authority to perform it.

instruction.heading: Where electrical work begins
instruction.body: Many handyman tasks look simple but touch fixed wiring: replacing a light fitting, adding a power point, moving a switch, mounting a wall fitting with a hard-wired feed, or fixing a socket that is loose. Treat any task that involves the fixed installation as a referral to a licensed electrical worker unless the state rules and your written authority clearly place it within your scope.

instruction.heading: The licence picture by state
instruction.body: In New South Wales, a licence or certificate is needed for wiring work whatever the price, and the NSW electrical page sets no dollar threshold (electrical page, last updated 23 June 2026). That page does not mention solar or battery systems. Energy Safe Victoria's renewable energy licence questions page (reviewed 4 June 2024) is UNVERIFIED for this lesson: the page was not fetched, so the claims that it covers inspection of battery and generation systems and does not name the class for installing or isolating PV are unconfirmed. These positions are a summary of what the sources say. They do not authorise any worker to carry out the work, and they must be checked with the regulator before a job is accepted.

instruction.heading: A suspected fault found on site
instruction.body: If you find a warm plug, scorched outlet, flickering light, burning smell, exposed conductor or a switchboard that is damaged, stop work near it. Do not open covers or touch exposed parts. Isolate the area from people where that is safe, and advise the occupant not to use the affected point. Record what you saw, where and when. Refer the fault to a licensed electrical worker and tell the approver in writing. Report the completed non-electrical work separately from the electrical referral, and do not mark the whole property safe.

instruction.heading: Everyday electrical tasks: state requirements
instruction.body: Replacing a light fitting, adding a power point, moving a switch, mounting a hard-wired wall fitting and fixing a loose socket are taught in this course for recognition, so you can spot them on a job and refer them correctly. Each one may be restricted by state law, so check the state note for the job location before you accept the task. In New South Wales, you must have an electrical licence or certificate before you can do any electrical wiring work, regardless of the cost of the work (electrical page, last updated 23 June 2026), so any of these tasks that involves wiring needs a person holding that licence or certificate. In Queensland, the QBCC handyman exemption does not cover electrical work, and the QBCC page directs electrical questions to the Electrical Safety Office, so confirm the Queensland electrical rule with that office before you start (QBCC page, last reviewed 11 August 2021). In Victoria, Energy Safe Victoria states that installation and maintenance of PV systems are required to be carried out by licensed electrical workers (page reviewed 15 April 2025). The sources for this lesson do not state the Victorian rule for light fittings or power points, so confirm it with Energy Safe Victoria first. The sources for this lesson do not cover South Australia, Western Australia, Tasmania, the Northern Territory or the Australian Capital Territory, so treat these tasks as referral work in those states until the state regulator confirms the position.

procedure: Identify whether the task touches the fixed installation, a switchboard, a fixed fitting or a power point.
If it does, stop and check the state position for electrical work in the matrix.
Refer the task to a licensed electrical worker and tell the approver in writing.
If a fault is seen during other work, stop near it, keep people away from exposed parts, and advise the occupant not to use the affected point.
Record the observation, location, time and the referral.
Report unrelated completed work separately from the electrical referral.

workedExamples.situation: While fitting a shelf, you find a power point that is scorched around the face plate and the occupant says it has been flickering.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Should you finish the shelf and tidy the power point?
workedExamples.reasoning: No. The scorched face plate and flickering suggest a fault in the fixed wiring. Stop near the power point, advise the occupant not to use it, record the observation, and refer to a licensed electrical worker. The shelf can be finished later when the power point has been dealt with, if the approver agrees, and the completion record must show the electrical referral.

equipmentAndPpe: Written work order showing the approved scope
Photo record device, used with consent
The state licence matrix for the job location

commonErrors.error: Replacing a light fitting or adding a power point as an ordinary handyman task.
commonErrors.prevention: Treat fixed-wiring changes as referral unless the state rules and written authority place them within your scope.

commonErrors.error: Tidying a scorched or flickering power point and moving on.
commonErrors.prevention: Stop, keep people away, advise the occupant not to use it, and refer.

commonErrors.error: Telling the client the whole property is electrically safe after a small repair.
commonErrors.prevention: Report only what was checked. Record the electrical referral separately.

commonErrors.error: Assuming a light fitting or power point is licence-free because the job is not in New South Wales or Victoria.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the state note for the job location. The sources for this lesson do not confirm a licence-free position for any state, and the Queensland and other-state notes require confirmation before the task starts.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: New South Wales: a licence or certificate is needed for wiring work whatever the cost, except for equipment at not more than 50 volts AC or 120 volts ripple-free DC (electrical page, last updated 23 June 2026). Mains-voltage solar or battery wiring is above that limit, and the NSW page does not mention solar or battery systems. This lesson does not grant that licence.
This lesson does not grant any licence for work on energy generation and storage systems.
Victoria: Energy Safe Victoria lists installation and maintenance of PV systems as electrical installation work that must be carried out by licensed electrical workers (page reviewed 15 April 2025).
Completing this lesson does not grant an electrical licence, a certificate, or any authority to perform electrical work.

Queensland: the QBCC handyman exemption does not cover electrical work, and the QBCC page directs electrical questions to the Electrical Safety Office (QBCC page, last reviewed 11 August 2021). This lesson does not state the Queensland electrical licence class.

Other states: the sources for this lesson do not cover South Australia, Western Australia, Tasmania, the Northern Territory or the Australian Capital Territory. Treat electrical tasks in those states as referral work until the state regulator confirms the position.

qualityStandard: Every task is checked against the state electrical position before any work starts.
Every suspected electrical fault is stopped, recorded and referred.
Completed non-electrical work is reported separately from any electrical referral.
documentationEvidence: Referral note naming the fault, the location, the time and the licensed trade
Written notice to the approver and the occupant
summary: Fixed wiring, switchboards and fixed fittings are referral work unless written authority and state rules place them within scope.
Stop and refer any suspected electrical fault, and keep people away from exposed parts.
The state licence positions are summaries and must be confirmed with the regulator before a job is accepted.

knowledgeChecks.question: A power point is scorched and the occupant says it has been flickering. What should you do?
options: Tighten the face plate and finish the shelf, since the point looks loose and the fix is quick and easy for the occupant
Open the cover to look at the wiring, since a quick check will show what is wrong with the point and the cable
Stop near the power point, advise the occupant not to use it, record the observation, and refer to a licensed electrical worker
Ignore it because the shelf is the task you were booked to finish today, and the point is not part of the booking at all

knowledgeChecks.question: According to the New South Wales source, when does electrical wiring work need a licence or certificate?
